title: I feel like if I released this during the NES era it would've been successful
author: getaway_golf
selftext: hired an artist who promised he wouldn't use ai, that turned out to be a lie. oh well, my game concept survived, is this just too boring? the comments seem to hate this game. how can I make it more addicting, I was going for metal gear solid meets mini golf.

comments.author: MiraculousMayhem
comments.body: Because the security guards have flashlights and seem to be actively looking, when they spot the ball in range of the flashlight, they should be alerted and hastily run towards the ball to capture it. The game looks fun though. I bet it would still successful on a browser or on mobile.

replies.author: getaway_golf
replies.body: They do currently chase, they just have loose targeting to keep it from being too hard for first time players. Speedrunning and never being detected at all is the goal.

replies.author: Party-Attorney-9681
replies.body:
The gaurd lights could

do an alert meter, it fills up an once full your out, this gives the torch some meaning, the meter could reset sometimes or be global so you can only spend some time in the light or...

the torchlights could push u or pull u, so this could mean when u try to bounce through the lights to a room the torches have gravity, e.g. some push, some pull, some are brighter, e.g. more push or pull. some slow u down, then create times when u have to go through three torches,e.g. slow torch, so u have to really power up the throw, second torch is a soft pull and the third is a strong push so the aim has to compensate to get through all three torches. pull torches eventually pull you to the gaurd, push torches might push u to a corner and the gaurd advances. 

Gaurds could also kick u, instead of kill u. makes it fun, you could get kicked into a situation u didnt want or you could expand on it and gaurds might kick you around the office back to the start on some maps if caught

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Honestly you'd have been better off just going with a primitive, vector art style focusing on lighting, colors and shapes. We've seen a bunch of those with puzzle games in recent years that have done extremely well. Abstract gfx often works better than clashing art styles. You do need to make this tremendously harder though imo if you want people to play it. Doesn't seem very challenging with the light spreads doing absolutely nothing. Outside of the fact there's a timer it doesn't really feel pressing, and even for that you could just spam little jumps over and over to move through quickly while limiting any chances of a guard encounter to virtually nothing. I think the success of games like Getting Over It (and other ragebaits) speak to the general craving of the audience and propensity for difficulty to take things viral.
